work: Bone, Lee, Narayanan - A Robust Unsupervised Arousal Rating Framework using Prosody with Cross-Corpora Evaluation
main_question: Can neutral speaker baselines and interpretable prosody produce robust unsupervised arousal ratings?
relation_to_ours: Very close: speaker-relative prosody; arousal; cross-corpus; small speaker reference
key_difference: Does not manipulate/decompose target reference frame or test when speaker normalization should vs should not be used

work: Busso, Mariooryad, Metallinou, Narayanan - Iterative Feature Normalization Scheme for Automatic Emotion Detection from Speech
main_question: Can neutral-speech normalization reduce inter-speaker variability while preserving emotion differences?
key_difference: Frames speaker variability mainly as nuisance; no target-reference intervention

work: Bone, Lee, Narayanan - Robust Unsupervised Arousal Rating: A Rule-Based Framework with Knowledge-Inspired Vocal Features
main_question: Can a speaker-baseline, rule-based vocal measure provide robust scale-continuous arousal ratings across corpora?
relation_to_ours: Closest procedural precursor: speaker baselines, relative vocal features, continuous arousal, cross-corpus robustness, limited labeled reference
key_difference: Does not manipulate target between/within-speaker structure or test representation-reference × target-reference coupling

work: Mariooryad, Busso - Compensating for speaker or lexical variabilities in speech for emotion recognition
main_question: Can speaker/lexical variability be factorized and compensated?

work: Wang & Maxwell - On disaggregating between-person and within-person effects with longitudinal data using multilevel models
main_question: How should centering separate within-person and between-person effects?
relation_to_ours: Establishes that person-mean centering / within-between decomposition is standard statistical methodology
key_difference: No speech representation or normalization-reference matching experiment

work: Sridhar, Parthasarathy, Busso - Role of Regularization in the Prediction of Valence from Speech
main_question: Why does valence need stronger regularization?
key_difference: Does not connect target speaker structure to normalization/reference-frame choice

work: Gat et al. - Speaker Normalization for Self-supervised Speech Emotion Recognition
main_question: Can adversarial speaker suppression improve SSL SER?
key_difference: Treats speaker information as shortcut/nuisance rather than conditional task information

work: Sridhar, Busso - Unsupervised Personalization of an Emotion Recognition System
main_question: Can valence models be personalized using acoustically similar speakers?
key_difference: Performance personalization rather than target-reference mechanism

work: Tran, Yin, Soleymani - Personalized Adaptation with Pre-trained Speech Encoders for Continuous Emotion Recognition
main_question: Can pretrained encoders and speaker calibration personalize continuous SER?
key_difference: Does not manipulate target reference frame

work: Lu et al. - Improving Speaker-Independent SER using Dynamic Joint Distribution Adaptation
main_question: Can speaker-domain adaptation learn speaker-invariant emotion features?
key_difference: Assumes speaker bias should be removed for generalization

work: Triantafyllopoulos, Schuller - Enrolment-based personalisation for improving individual-level fairness in SER
main_question: Can small speaker enrollment improve personalization/fairness?
key_difference: Enrollment is for personalization; no Absolute/Relative target-frame mechanism

work: Ulgen, Du, Busso, Sisman - Revealing Emotional Clusters in Speaker Embeddings
main_question: Do speaker embeddings contain useful emotion clusters?
key_difference: Does not study feature/target reference-frame matching

work: Shi, Li, Toda - Speaker-Aware Multi-Task Learning for SER
main_question: Can speaker-aware multitask modeling improve SER?
